blocks.text: Laura spat.

The small orange shot cut through the taut joining rope and scorched the nearest wrist turns. She wrenched her hands apart, tearing the blackened fibers. Another quick shot burned the rope across her coat. She dragged an arm free, shrugged out of the loosened loops and scrambled up.
Daniel stepped into her path. Laura flicked a small shot at the loose hem of his lab coat. The cloth flared.
blocks.alt: Laura steps free of the rooftop vent, her wrists unbound and cut rope pieces discarded beside her boots.

blocks.text: He recoiled, tore the coat off and stamped out the flame, retreating toward the stairhouse.
blocks.alt: Dork recoils from his discarded lab coat’s flaming hem, backing toward the stairhouse in his gray shirt and dark tie.

blocks.text: She was already moving.
Luke darted across her path, iron teeth snapping. Laura ducked past him and lunged for the collector.
“Don’t touch the machine, Laura. It’s too dangerous.”
Flaming Head’s warning reached her mind alone. Daniel and Luke heard nothing.
She seized the brass rim and the trolley’s upper rail.
Pain shot through her hands. Orange light flared beneath her gloves and ran up her arms. She tried to let go, but her fingers would not open.
Inside the glass, Flaming Head struggled toward her. The pull swept him back.

Laura threw her weight against the rail. The wheels jammed against their chocks. The trolley rocked, one corner lifting off the roof, and a bright thread of fire streamed from her mouth into the funnel.
She could not scream. It was taking the heat out of her throat.
Luke wheeled toward the western controls. The storage needle was still climbing. His chance of getting a body was inside that glass, and she was tipping it over.
He clamped his iron jaw over the control box’s upper edge and drove forward against her shove.
blocks.alt: Laura grips the active collector’s brass rim and rail in pain while her orange energy is drawn into the intake; Flaming Head remains trapped inside.

blocks.text: The housing buckled. Both needles slammed against their stops.
The collector exploded.
White light burst from the western panel. The blast tore Luke away and hurled him backward across the clear strip toward the warehouse wall.
blocks.alt: Luke braces his iron jaw against the collector’s control housing as its stored energy erupts into an electrical explosion.

blocks.text: Luke struck the bricked-up window.
Mortar burst around his head. Bricks broke inward, and he vanished through the opening in a cloud of dust.
The collector went dark. Both needles fell.
Laura’s hands came free. She stumbled backward as the raised corner slammed down. The glass split between the copper coils, spilling sparks across the roof.
A small orange flame escaped through the brass mouth and drifted low above the roof.
Daniel emerged from behind the stairhouse and hurried to the broken window. Beyond the opening, Luke lay motionless among the bricks on the warehouse floor. Daniel peered through the settling dust.
Luke did not stir.
blocks.alt: Luke’s steel-jawed head breaks through the established bricked-up warehouse window as the collector shuts down.

blocks.text: Laura sank beside the vent, holding her hands against her coat.
Flaming Head came down in front of her. His crest was barely higher than his brow.
“Thank you.”
The words were faint inside her mind. Across the roof, Daniel remained bent through the broken window. He could not hear Flaming Head.
Laura swallowed. Her throat felt cool, but the sight of his shrunken flame made her stomach twist. He had come because she had asked. She could hardly look at him.
“I helped him do this to you. I’m so sorry.”
There was no anger in the warmth that reached her.
“You chose to help me. I’m proud of you, Laura. I’ll keep you safe.”
The connection faded with the words. She could still see him, but the familiar warmth inside her was gone.
Dust tickled her nose.
Laura clapped a gloved hand over her mouth and turned away.
She sneezed.
For an instant she stayed frozen, waiting for the burn.
Her glove was damp. The fabric was whole. Nothing smoked.
She stared at it, then let out a shaky laugh. Another sneeze caught her before she could stop it. An ordinary, ridiculous sneeze.
She was laughing and crying now, wiping her nose with the back of her glove.
blocks.alt: Freed of her power, Laura laughs through tears at an ordinary harmless sneeze while weakened Flaming Head stays close.

blocks.text: Flaming Head hovered close while she stood. Laura took off the mask and tucked it into her coat pocket.
Luke was still motionless beyond the broken wall when she reached the stairs.
She wanted to go home. For the first time in months, that was all she had to do.
